report:
Reviewed the complete rustc_lints claim and both ordinary associated tests after adding explicit naming-lint coverage and implementation associations. There are no TODO/N/A entries. Requirements: individually allow warning-by-default lints from the pinned compiler inventory; suppress incidental unused-item and naming warnings; preserve deny-by-default lints; permit source attributes to enable or deny warnings; require emitted warnings/errors to match markers; avoid a lint cap and preserve hard language errors.
Implementation: both rustc.rs associations are substantive. quiet_lints invokes the same metadata::our_rustc binary as check with -W help, selects rows whose default level is warn, excludes the aggregate warnings group, produces individual -A flags, rejects an inventory without dead-code, and caches the result. Deny/default-allow entries are untouched. check appends these flags to the ordinary compilation command, with no --cap-lints. The new execute/validate_output extraction preserves this path and passes structured diagnostics to matching. The metadata association resolves bin/rustc under the embedded sysroot; captured build.rs shows how that sysroot is embedded. The observe association enforces exhaustive severity/location matching of the applicable ERROR/WARN markers, rejecting unconsumed diagnostics or markers. Captured annotation parsing confirms WARN/ERROR and rustc conditions; captured CompileTest preparation confirms the result is propagated to the caller.
Tests: pinned_rustc_checks_errors_editions_and_normal_library_configuration rejects an unmarked bool-to-u8 hard type error, accepts the matching ERROR, and accepts a marked out-of-range u8 literal, establishing that the deny-by-default overflowing_literals error survives. Its unused ordinary functions also exercise default quiet behavior; edition and library-configuration cases supply additional related execution coverage. rustc_is_mandatory_and_warnings_can_be_enabled_in_source now prepares both unused and nonSnakeCase functions without markers, exercising both named incidental warning families. Its explicit warn(dead_code) without marker fails with exactly one rustc diagnostic, the corresponding WARN marker succeeds, and deny(dead_code) with ERROR succeeds. These positive/negative assertions distinguish individual allows from a blanket lint cap and establish source overrides and required markers.
Validation actually executed: cargo fmt; cargo build (passed with existing sage-ir warnings); cargo test -p sage-test-harness --lib rustc_ after final shared edits (4 passed, including both associated tests). Source inspection and these focused runs support approval; no claim is made that the entire workspace test suite ran in this reviewer.
